titulo: Living with an API that changes: watch the spec, Chrome Status and the MCP changelog
lead: The WebMCP API has already moved once: from navigator to document. It will change again before any stable release. Instead of finding out from a visitor, record what the sources said on the day the test suite passed and let a script compare. Changed? Run the test suite and read it before touching anything.
objetivo: record the baseline from the day the test suite passed and watch the spec, Chrome Status and MCP, with the navigator → document case as an example.

aprende.t: The timeline of the navigator → document switch

secoes.titulo: An API that has already changed
secoes.sub: Dates read from primary sources on 10/19/2026. Click each milestone.

nos.detalhe: In the first drafts, the API lived at navigator.modelContext. Today that is the old name: don't teach it or copy it.
PR #177, "Scope ModelContext to Document", accepted on 05/19/2026: the API moves to document.modelContext.
Chrome origin trial post on 06/09/2026; Chrome Status: origin trial from 149 to 156, status "Proposed", no stable date.
Draft Community Group Report from 10/16/2026: registerTool, getTools, executeTool, and the toolchange event. No unregisterTool, provideContext, or clearContext.
vigia/base.json: what the sources said on the day YOUR battery passed (in the kit, 10/19/2026).
vigiar.mjs reads the sources again and compares them with the baseline. Same: nothing to do. Changed: exit 1, run the battery (lesson 4) and read the change.

secoes.sub: Public pages, no key and no cost.

texto: The date at the top of the draft and the IDL names (registerTool, getTools, executeTool, toolchange).
Old name coming back or a new method showing up: time to reread.
The status ("Proposed" on 10/19/2026) and the origin trial versions (149 to 156).
The trial ends at 156: note it in your calendar, along with the token.
The versioning page gives the current revision (2026-07-28) and the changelog says what changed.
The Registry is in preview, with a notice of changes and resets: don't depend on it.
The kit's server answers server/discover with the revisions it speaks (2026-07-28).
Package version always pinned; upgrading is a decision, with the battery first.

secoes.titulo: Compare with the old course's baseline
secoes.sub: A baseline with only what the old course recorded (spec date and surface). The rest shows up as "sem base".
Watch, see a real change, and save your own baseline. Each exercise ends in a done when.

exercicios.titulo: E1 · Watch against the kit's baseline
exercicios.texto: Run the watch. If MUDOU shows up, note what it says: that is the warning working.
exercicios.pronto: node scripts/vigiar.mjs; echo "saída: $?" → VIGIA: 7/7 iguais à base · nada a fazer and saída: 0 as long as nothing has changed since 10/19/2026; with a change, MUDOU lines and saída: 1.

exercicios.titulo: E2 · The change the old course missed
exercicios.texto: Run the watch against the 09/24/2026 baseline.
After the battery passes on your project (lesson 4), save your baseline and mark the next watch and the end of the origin trial (Chrome 156) on your calendar.
exercicios.pronto: node scripts/vigiar.mjs --base vigia/minha-base.json --gravar → base gravada em vigia/minha-base.json, and the calendar has both dates.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after the answer.

perguntas.p: The watch came back with MUDOU spec_data. What is the right order?
opcoes: Re-freeze the battery right away, so it does not block the deploy in the queue.
Save the new baseline and move on: the date alone does not matter.
Run the battery, read what changed, and only then fix or re-freeze.
Remove WebMCP from the site until the stable version ships.
perguntas.explica: A change in the source calls for proof (the battery) and reading. Re-freezing or re-saving the baseline without reading erases the warning; removing everything is overkill, since the fallback already protects the visitor.

perguntas.p: Why does navigator.modelContext appear in this lesson?
opcoes: It is the old name, replaced by PR #177 on 05/19/2026: a real case of change.
It is the current name in Chrome, and document.modelContext is just the name the polyfill uses.
It is the name Chrome Status uses for the origin trial.
It is the nickname the 10/16/2026 spec keeps for compatibility.
perguntas.explica: The 10/16/2026 spec only has document.modelContext. The old name serves as an example of an API that changes; in Chromium 156 it does not exist (measured in the kit).

perguntas.p: The watch exited with 3 ("SEM CONCLUSÃO"). What does that mean?
opcoes: Three sources changed since the baseline.
The spec has become stable and the watch can be turned off for good.
The baseline is corrupted and needs to be deleted.
There was no network to read the sources; nothing was compared.
perguntas.explica: Without reading the sources, the watch says nothing, and code 3 sets this apart from "same" (0) and "changed" (1).

perguntas.p: Why not depend on the MCP Registry in production today?
opcoes: Because it only accepts servers on the 2025-11-25 revision.
Because it is in preview, with a warning about changes and data resets.
Because it requires the WebMCP origin trial in Chrome.
Because it replaces server/discover from the new revision.
perguntas.explica: The Registry's own site says "currently in preview" and warns of breaking changes and resets. Publishing there can be useful; depending on it, no.

itens.texto: The API has already switched from navigator to document and will change again before any stable release.
Save what the sources said on the day the battery passed.
It changed: battery, reading, fix; only then are the baseline and the battery re-saved.
